>i ANNUAL REPORT 


In reviewing the record of the work accomplished during another 
year, we cannot do so without first acknowledging the mercy and grace of 
our God, and confessing with deep humiliation the unfaithfulness of those 
who have been permitted to share in the joy of His service. For all that 
has been accomplished, we render the praise and honor to Him who liveth 
and reigneth forever and ever. . 


We cannot proceed further without referring with deep regret, to the 
loss we have sustained by the resignation in June last, of our esteemed 
President, Mr. T. JAMES CLAXTON, who has been so actively identified 
with the history of the Association since its inception—twenty-eight years 
ago, —as well as with the general work on this continent. The Committee 
delayed its acceptance at first, and urged him to allow his name to remain 
until the close of the year. This, however, he distinctly declined, leaving 
them no alternative but to accept his resignation. In the meantime, the 
Vice-Presidents have fulfilled the duties of the office. 


The general depression in all branches of industry has now existed 
so long as to greatly affect that class of the community we are specially 
established to reach. Through the failure of so many firms, and the con- 
sequent reduction of staffs and salaries our membership list has suffered 
great loss. One hundred and twenty-seven letters of introduction have 
been granted to young men passing to other Associations, and from the 
same cause not a few are unable to pay their annual fee. 


The roll at present stands as follows :— 


List of Members.

Active members are urged to give more diligence to the enrolment 
of new members. 

The distinctive religious work of the Association which seeks the 
spiritual welfare of young men, demands and receives the first place.

8 


BOYS’ MEETING, FRIDAY at 8 P.M. 


Owing to the Leader’s enforced absence, this Meeting has latterly fallen off 
somewhat, but an effort is now being made to revive it. and doubtless it 
will regain its former interest. 


SUNDAY SCHOOL TEACHERS’ MEETING 
SATURDAY at NOON. 


This opportunity of reviewing the lesson before teaching, has been much 
appreciated by many Teachers. The Class has been conducted by the - 
Rev. Mr. Wells, Rev. Canon Baldwin, Principal Dawson, Rev. Mr. Munro, © 
Rey. Mr. Johnston, Rev. Mr. McCaul, for a month at a time; it was 
suspended during the summer months, and now resumed, Canon Baldwin 
having taken October, the Rev. J. S. Black, November. It will be con- 
tinued throughout the Winter. Attendance from 60 to 100. 


YOUNG MEN’S EVANGELISTIC MEETING. 
SATURDAY EVENING at 8. 


This Meeting continues to be a source of blessing to many, and the good 
attendance is very much due to the faithfulness of the Invitation Committee, 
who distribute slips of invitation through the streets, prior to the Meetings. 
There is ample room however, for a much larger representation of our 
Members, and it is desirable that it should be more generally regarded as 
a Meeting which ought to be regularly attended. ‘There are constantly 
enquirers, amongst a number, the following instance of conversion may be 
given :— 


A young Englishman, who had visited many countries, and found 
neither success nor satisfaction, arrived in Montreal last June ; through 
the Association he was introduced to a boarding house, and afterwards a 
situation procured for him, although clothed with the righteousness of 
morality, the spirit of God through the testimony His children, convinced 
him of his great need, and the truth made him a free man in Christ Jesus. 
Shortly afterwards he was removed to a neighboring City, and in writing 
he says : 


‘* My desire to roam from place has been changed and I am contented 
to remain where my lot is cast, the joy of realizing God to be a ersonal 
friend, is very great, and the consciousness of receiving answers to prayer 
and strength to overcome sinful habits is precious beyond my power to 
express,” &c. 


9 


Another young man who likewise has been made free by receiving 
the glad news of pardon and peace through Christ Jesus, sends the message 
to his christian praying mother, a widow, the return mail brings the 


joyous reply : 


‘* Your letter yesterday brings such joyful news, that I cannot express 
my happiness and gratitude, for God has indeed answered my prayers and 
guided you into the path of peace. I praise Him with all my heart, for 
now I know your future is safe. Do not delay to connect yourself with 
some Church, and ask dazly for the guidance of His Spirit, that you may 
live to the glory of Him who has redeemed you with His blood.” &e. 


A man of middle age who for years had vainly endeavoured to satisfy 
his conscience with an zzellectual acceptance of God’s truth (according to 
the teaching of certain schools), found in such belief no power to overcome 
evil habits. He was through a friend induced to come to this Meeting, 
and by the power of the Spirit of God, led to a heart-belief which he 
gladly confesses, has given him a new life and a new power over self 


and sin. 


Still another, a farmer from the Far West, who found his way to 
the Meetings, and under God found his need of a personal knowledge of 
acceptance in Christ, now that he has gone away writes that, ‘‘The 
return of each Saturday evening, brings him into fellowship (in spirit) 
with the young men where he received so much blessing at the hand of 


God.” 


Instances might be multiplied, but these will suffice to show that 
while permitted to sow the seed, the laborers through the mercy of God, 
are also allowed to share in the joy of the harvest, the fulness of which 
will only be known, however, at the time of the Gathering Home. The 
attendance at this Meeting runs from 50 to 7 5. 


Early in the year Meetings were held in the Hall, by Mr. CROMBIE 
which were used: under God in leading souls to Christ. The Association 
also derived much benefit from the visit of the REv. Mr. PARSONS, of 
Buffalo, N.Y., while later on also from a visit of Mr. Hopper of the 
Parent Association, and Mr. FeRMAUD of Geneva, Switzerland, Secretary 
of the Associations of all Lands. On the invitation of the Association, 
Mr. Gro. MULLER, of Bristol, England, visited the City and spent a few 
days holding services in different Churches, many christians received fresh 
stimulus to prayer and the study of God’s word from his earnest addresses. 


B 


10 


During the Week of Prayer for Young Men, Special 
Meetings were held each day at Noon, and some 15 of our City Pastors 
preached Special Sermons on the Sunday. 


On Xmas Morning an enjoyable Praise Meeting was held, 
and likewise on the evening of Thanksgiving Day a well-attended 
Meeting for Thanksgiving. 


OTHER MEETINGS. 


On NEw YEAR’s EVENING a Supper was given in the Reading Room, 
to about 120 News-Boys, their behaviour was excellent. The hearty 
way in which the Boys appreciated and enjoyed everything, was something 
to be long remembered 


For the SArItors oF H.M.S. ‘‘TOURMALINE”’, a Social was also 
arranged, some 40 or 50 of the men came; the Rev. Mr. Wells and 
others, gave short practical addresses; lady friends provided refreshments 
and a boquet of flowers for each Sailor; the music was chiefly provided 
by the men themselves ; altogether it seemed a time of great enjoyment 
for the ‘‘ Tars” and apparently appreciated by them. It was hoped by 
thus making the Rooms a point of attraction for the Sailors, to counteract 
some of the many zzjfluences for evil which surround /ack ashore. 


Lectures, &c. The Association has to record its indebtedness to 
Drs. Buller, Blackadder, Kelley and Roddick, to the Rev. Geo. Wells, as 
also to Principal Dawson, and Mr. Geo. Hague, for their great kindness 
in delivering Lectures during last Winter. At the request of many the 
Lecture of the last named gentleman, on ‘‘ Modern Business,” was printed in 
pamphlet form for circulation. 


For the WINTER SEASON 1879-’80, the Committee has arranged a 
series of fortnightly Socials and Lectures (alternating) to be held on 
Thursday Evenings.. These are for Alembers and their friends, and it is 
hoped by the attractive Programme issued, not only to provide such 
Social and Intellectual re-union for Members as God’s blessing can be 
invoked upon, but also thereby to interest others in the work of the 
Association, who at present are not reached. It will be the endeavour to 
keep prominently in view, the essentially Crzstzan character of the work, _ 
and to that end, at these Social Meetings some phase of the Association’s . | 
sphere of labor, will always be taken up in an address, q

THE MISSION COMMITTEE 


During the past year, have been permitted to engage in the following 
branches of christian work :—The holding of Cottage and Gospel 
Meetings, Hospital and Gaol Services, and meetings amongst the Fire- 
men and Sailors. 

About fifty of the members have been thus engaged under the direc- 
tion of the Committee, and they desire to acknowledge with thankfulness 
the blessings they have personally received, and rejoice in the knowledge 
that the labor has not been in vain, 


The following are particulars of different Meetings :— 


Place of Meeting. Number of Meetings. Total Attendance.

It will thus be seen that 351 meetings were held with a total attend- 
ance of 5,143, not including the workers. 

Hospital.—The average attendance at the Hospital was 11 patients 

and 3 workers to each meeting. When opportunity offers some of the 


12 


Wards are also visited. One of the members also visits three times a week, 
going from patient to patient, and God has richly blessed his labors, 
We have every reason to believe that from these services souls have been 
‘* born again.” 


Sailors’ Institute.—The Prayer Meetings were commenced 
on Monday, May 2oth, and have been held every Monday, Tuesday, 
Wednesday and Thursday Evenings, during the season, and proved a 
means of blessing to many souls. The Christian Sailors have taken an 
active part in testimony and prayer, and have thus been made to feel it 
was their Meeting. God’s children have been built up in their most 
holy faith, and many have given evidence of having passed from death 
unto life. A christian Captain said that three of his crew had been led — 
to the Lord through this instrumentality. We doubt not but that many 
others were also blessed. These men during this winter will be sailing 
to different ports, and will be meeting with new shipmates, and old ones 
not seen for some time, may God give them grace to testify of the blessing 
received, and may they be the means of winning others to Christ. As 
a result, the Sunday Services conducted by Mr. Ritchie have been largely 
increased, both in interest and attendance, through the week-night ser- 
vices. 


Gaol.—tThe first meeting in the Gaol was held on Sunday, the 
12th October, about 4o being present. Short addresses were given, 
and several hymns sung, which seemed to be much appreciated. The 
attendance is now from seventy to eighty. It is difficult to carry on this 
work successfully, the time allotted, 1.30 p.m., is inconvenient, as 
the workers have duties to attend to at 3 o’clock, and it does not give 
them opportunity for personal conversation, which is much desired, and 
essential to all successful work. We trust however that a way will be 
opened for a change in the hour. 


DISTRIBUTION OF RELIGIOUS READING, 


Sailors.—Each Sunday morning during the summer a number 
of our members have visited all the ships in the harbor, and distributed 
tracts and illustrated papers. They are universally received with the 
greatest kindness, and frequent opportunities occur for religious conver- 
sation. | 

Firemen.—The Sunday evening meetings in the stations have 
been discontinued, but will doubtless he renewed if the way is opened. 
The Committee, however, still continue to distribute magazines and 
papers at each station every Sunday morning, and their visits are thank- 
fully received. 


— 


13 


In order to continue this work effectually amongst the Firemen, 
Sailors, and at the Hospital and Gaol, we are in constant need of maga- 
zines, periodicals, illustrated papers, &c., and any friends having a stock 
Jaid aside will confer a favor by sending their names to the Secretary. 
Many of the Sunday Schools, as well as friends, have contributed last 


year, to whom the Committee now desire to return their thanks. 
? 
Expenses.—The amount incurred in carrying on the work of 


the Mission Committee has been $101.73, which has, by the kindness of 
friends, all been paid, and your Committee retire free of debt. 

Before closing this Report we would bear testimony to labors of 
Brother W. P. Crombie in connection with the Nazareth Street meet- 
ing. During the past winter he conducted services there for some weeks, 
and God owned and blessed him to the conversion of precious souls. 


THE INVITATION COMMITTEE 


has virtually been without a Chairman during the past year, but have 
unremittingly continued their work. On Saturday evening, at. 7.30, from 
eight to ten assemble, and after prayer, visit the Hotels, and are stationed 
on the leading thoroughfares. The slips distributed not only contain an 
invitation to attend the meetings, but striking Scripture texts, many of 
which doubtless bear fruit, although unheard of by the workers. There is, 
however, an abundance of direct results, which greatly encourages the 
Committee. 

Besides this, the following Card has been distributed to guests at the 
Hotels, remaining over Sunday, their names being ascertained from the 
Register.

EVERY NIGHT MISSION 


has been commenced in a Hall, No. 712 Craig Street. The funds neces- 
sary to continue the work throughout the winter have already been sub- 
scribed. Two of our members are responsible for the conduct of the 
meeting each evening, and several ladies have kindly consented to aid 
in the Service of Song. The workers have faith to believe that this Mis- 
sion will be greatly blessed. 


A Committee is being formed to supply religious services in adjacent 
localities which are destitute of Church privileges. Two stations are now 
being supplied weekly. Volunteers are required for this work. 


THE FINANCE COMMITTEE 


gratefully acknowledge the goodness of God in placing means in their 
hands for carrying on the various departments of our Association Work 
through another year. Although the year just closing has been character- 
ized, like its predecessor, with depression in many branches of trade, yet 
we are glad to be able to record, that the receipts from subscriptions and 
donations have increased during this year. The fees from membership 
have decreased, owing to the fact that many have left the city, and many 
others are unable to pay, from lack of employment. 


When your Committee entered office, twelve months ago, they found 
outstanding debts against the Association to the amount of $2,300, which 
had been allowed to accumulate during previous years. Special efforts 

were made to pay off these claims, but with only partial success.- We 
close this year with a debt of $1,950 on general expenses, &c. 


THE DEBT ON THE BUILDING will be reduced another $5000.00 in a 
few weeks, and we appeal to any who may not have had the Peyilcen of 
subscribing to this fund, to come forward and help us. 


THE CURRENT EXPENSES have been considerably reduced in all 
departments of our work during the past year. It is due to the untir- 
ing efforts of our Treasurer, Mr. J. S. McLachlan, under the blessing of 
God, that we find ourselves in so good a position to-day. 


We would again record our earnest conviction, that a body of sustain- 
tng Members should be raised, who would agree to give annually, say a 
sum of $5 or $10, and thus afford to the Finance Committee a regular 
and assured source of income, and relieve the Treasurer of much 
anxiety. If we can truly engage in our Association Work, as being Christ’s 
Work, are we not called upon, as Members, to make sacrifice forit. Our 
blessed Lord died for us, and redeemed us to Himself, and shall we not 


ee re See 7 tee eae 


15 


give him our talents, time, and means. ‘‘7 beseech you therefore, brethren, 
by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living Sacrifice, 
holy, acceptable to God, which ts your reasonable seevice.” Let us seek a 
closer fellowship with Christ, in our everyday life, and we shall then 
know how to give to His cause. 


THE RECEPTION COMMITTEE 


consisting of ten members, was organized for work last December, a 
plan was drawn up by which Members would be in attendance at the 
Rooms from eight to ten o’clock each evening of the week, except Satur- 
day, to welcome strangers, receive visitors, speak with the anxious, and 
in every way endeavor to drop ‘‘a word in season,” 


The Members of the Committee were punctual and regular in their 
attendance during the early part of the year, but during the summer 
months both attendance and interest flagged. 


The number visiting the Rooms each evening varies from twenty-five 
to sixty, many of them being regular attendants. An illuminated sign 
will soon be placed outside the building and it is hoped that this will 
attract more visitors to our Rooms, especially strangers, and those 
unreached by other Christian effort. It has been found difficult to close 
the Rooms each evening with prayer, owing to the lack of a Chairman. 


The results of this work are perhaps not apparent, but it is enough 
for us to be faithful and diligent, leaving the results with God, our duty 
is to be ‘‘ always abounding in the work of the Lord, for as much as we 
know that our labor is not in vain in the Lord.” 


THE READING ROOM 


is supplied with 13 daily papers, 53 Secular and Religious Weeklies, 
23 Monthlies, and 3 Quarterly Reviews, including the most prominent 
English and American publications. It is well patronized, the average 
daily attendance being from 250 to 400 readers. It is not only a great 
benefit to our Members, but to strangers, and young men out of employ- 
ment. 


THE CIRCULATING LIBRARY 


has been but little used on account of the ancient character of the books 
on the shelves. For this reason we are continually losing Members, and 
it is to be hoped that the Finance Committee will be able to set aside a 
grant for this purpose at an early date, and thus meet a most pressing 
need. 


16 


THE REFERENCE LIBRARY 


is constantly used, but some kind friend could supply a great boon to our 
Members by filling its vacant shelves with the Standard Works of Refer- 
ence. Who will volunteer ? 


The Reading Room and Libraries were thoroughly cleaned and tint- 
-ed during the summer, and next year a new carpet will be required, the 
present one having done more than ordinary service. 


THE VISITATION OF THE SICK 


receives careful attention, not only in the Hospital, as previously men- 
tioned, but Members and others outside are regularly visited by the Sec- 
retary or some of the Members. 


EMPLOYMENT BUREAU. 


We are lacking in the effective working of this branch, as it requires 
more time than volunteer workers can devote to it. Out of the large num- 
ber of applications we have succeeded in securing //ty-seven situations 
during the year, not including temporary work which has been granted to 
a great number. In New York a retired merchant devotes two hours 
daily to this department. The importance of this is so great, it is hoped — 
that a Committee may be secured who can give to it the needful attention. 


A BOARDING HOUSE REGISTER 


is supplied with a list of carefully selected houses, and is daily consulted. 

-This is important, as we are not only able to direct young men tosuitable 
houses, but it brings us in personal contact with them, and furnishes us 
with their address, when we invariably acquint them with our meetings 
and work. 


THE SECRETARY’S WORK 


is intimately connected with all the other departments. Zhe Correspond- 
ence is daily increasing, and letters of enquiry are received from all sec- 
tions—no less than 174 on Association business, having been written 
during October. The ersonal calls for counsel in difficulty and friendly | 
advice, occupy much time and require careful and faithful attention. 
The providing of zemporary relief for those in straightened circumstances 
requires divine wisdom. ‘The deserving calls have been very numerous. 
Any assistance thus rendered has not been a tax upon the Treasurer, but 


4 


‘ 17 


contributed through the kindness of a few Members. There is not only 
room, but the greatest need to enlarge this circle, and volunteers are re- 


quested. 

A Pledge Book is kept in the Office, and 347 signatures have 
been added during the year. This is specially desirable as it affords an 
opportunity of personal religious conversation with so many men, and 
instances are known where some have been led into perfect liberty 


through Christ. 

Personal Effort should be the outcome of all branches of the 
work, for if our individual responsibility to God be not realized, surely no 
blessing can come to us, and therefore we cannot communicate to others 
that which we have mot- received. The danger ever to be avoided is to 
place dependence upon mere organization; to be taken up with 
the work of God, rather than in what He is to us, and our: individual 
relationship to Him. Systematized work is absolutely essential to any 
degree of success, but the POWER belongeth to God, and He gives freely 
to those who wait upon Him. While discountenancing any such legal 
bondage as would render it necessary that we speak to at least one indi- 
vidual daily about his spiritual welfare, we would urge each worker to 
seek that abiding union with Christ, and that fulness of the Spirit w hich 
will be an unerring guide as to his whole duty to his fellow-man. 


We cannot conclude this brief review without thanking and praising 
God that He has honored us with the great privilege of sharing in His 
glory, and of being the channel through which His blessings have been 
conveyed to many hearts, for we know that by the grace of God homes 
have been made happy, hearts have been made glad, the slaves to passion 
and vice have been restrained, the sick have been cheered and comforted, 
God’s Word has been honored and His name glorified, and His child- 
ren encouraged and blessed. 


D. A. BUDGE, 


Secretary.
